finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::sql statement injection: validateselectquery validates a comment-stripped copy of the query, but executequery interpolates the original string into a simple-protocol query, so ddl/dml can be smuggled past the read-only guard
evidence: I traced the payload through both files as supplied. sql-validator.ts strips `--...` to end-of-line with a regex that is unaware of double-quoted identifiers, and every subsequent check (first token, FORBIDDEN_KEYWORDS loop, `;` split) runs only on that stripped copy, while datasource.service.ts:148 interpolates the untouched `dto.query` into `SELECT * FROM (${dto.query}) AS _q LIMIT 10001`. For `SELECT 1 AS "x--" ) AS q; DROP TABLE users; SELECT * FROM (SELECT 1`, the validator sees only `SELECT 1 AS "x` (passes all checks), whereas Postgres treats `--` inside the double-quoted identifier as literal text and receives three complete statements; node-postgres sends a value-less string via the simple query protocol, which does execute multiple `;`-separated statements. The claim also correctly notes this is pre-existing and untested (sql-validator.spec.ts only covers the naive `SELECT 1; DROP TABLE users` case), and nothing in this diff closes it.
